scenes.heading: Simplifying and expanding expressions
scenes.sub: Tidy up algebra before you solve it
scenes.say: Before you can solve equations, you need tidy expressions. Today you will collect like terms, multiply terms, and remove brackets, including the tricky negative ones.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A postie drops letters at EVERY house in the street
scenes.science: The number outside a bracket multiplies EVERY term inside
scenes.breaks: a postie never delivers negative letters, but a negative outside changes the sign of every term inside.
scenes.say: Think of a postie who must drop letters at every house in the street, not just the first one. The number outside a bracket is that postie. In three, open bracket, two x plus five, the three must visit the two x and the five.

scenes.heading: Like terms
points: x² and x are NOT like terms
scenes.say: Like terms have exactly the same pronumerals with the same powers. Four x and negative seven x are like terms. x squared and x are not. And three a b and five b a are like terms, because a b equals b a. Add or subtract the numbers in front, and keep the letters.
scenes.caption: Like terms have exactly the same pronumerals with the same powers. 4x and −7x are like terms. x² and x are not. 3ab and 5ba are like terms, because ab = ba. Add or subtract the numbers in front, and keep the letters.

scenes.heading: Why 3(2x + 5) = 6x + 15
scenes.say: Here is a rectangle three high and two x plus five wide. First the two pieces, then their areas. The left piece is three by two x, so six x. The right piece is three by five, so fifteen. Together, six x plus fifteen.
scenes.caption: A rectangle 3 high and (2x + 5) wide. The left piece is 3 by 2x, so 6x. The right piece is 3 by 5, so 15. Together, 6x + 15.

scenes.heading: A negative outside
scenes.question: Expand −2(3x − 5).
scenes.say: Expand negative two, open bracket, three x minus five. Negative two times three x is negative six x. Negative two times negative five is positive ten. So the answer is negative six x plus ten.
scenes.caption: Expand −2(3x − 5). −2 × 3x = −6x. −2 × −5 = +10. So the answer is −6x + 10.

scenes.heading: Expand, then simplify
scenes.question: Expand and simplify 3(2x + 4) − 2(x − 5).
scenes.say: Expand both brackets first. Three times two x plus four gives six x plus twelve. Negative two times x minus five gives negative two x plus ten. Now collect like terms: four x plus twenty-two.
scenes.caption: Expand both brackets first: 6x + 12 and −2x + 10. Now collect like terms: 4x + 22.

scenes.heading: Multiplying and dividing terms
scenes.question: Simplify 3a × (−4ab) and 18x²y ÷ 6xy.
scenes.say: To multiply terms, multiply the numbers, then the letters. Three times negative four is negative twelve, and a times a b is a squared b. To divide, cancel. Eighteen divided by six is three, x squared divided by x is x, and the y terms cancel. So three x.
scenes.caption: To multiply terms, multiply the numbers, then the letters: −12a²b. To divide, cancel: 18 ÷ 6 = 3, x² ÷ x = x, and the y terms cancel. So 3x.

scenes.say: Quick recap. Only like terms combine. Multiply numbers, then pronumerals. The number outside visits every term, and a negative flips each sign. Check by substituting a number. Now try the practice questions!
